n2554a8dae09.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Deep Ocean Mission?
o: It is one of the nine PM-STIAC missions.
It excludes ocean energy and freshwater-related activities.
Its focus areas include deep-sea mining and a manned submersible.
Ocean biodiversity and ocean survey are among its focus areas.
n2554a8dae09.x: Ocean energy and freshwater are also among the mission's focus areas, so saying it excludes them is false; the other three are correct.

nf726e816d2e.s:
Assertion (A): UNCLOS set up the International Seabed Authority to regulate seabed mining beyond national jurisdiction.
Reason (R): UNCLOS was adopted in 1982 and came into force in 1994.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nf726e816d2e.x: UNCLOS did create the ISA for seabed mining beyond national jurisdiction, and it dates from 1982 (in force 1994); but its dates do not explain why it created the ISA.

n532803f34d6.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: only one dated fact)
n532803f34d6.s: Which is the nodal ministry for India's Deep Ocean Mission?
o: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
n532803f34d6.x: The Deep Ocean Mission (approved June 2021, ₹4,077 crore) is run by the Ministry of Earth Sciences, not the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

n32d65d9d897.s: The first tranche of offshore mineral blocks auctioned under a composite licence (November 2024) had how many blocks?
n32d65d9d897.x: The first tranche, auctioned on 28 November 2024 under the OAMDR Act, had 13 offshore blocks offered under a composite licence.

n7ed94f7fdac.s: The north-west Pacific fishing ground is associated with the meeting of which currents?
n7ed94f7fdac.x: The north-west Pacific fishing ground lies where the Kuroshio and Oyashio meet; the Gulf Stream-Labrador meeting is the Grand Banks.

nbdee2d5a91b.s: The annual mechanised fishing ban in India's territorial waters lasts how many days?
nbdee2d5a91b.x: Territorial-water fisheries (0-12 nm) are a State subject, with an annual two-month (61-day) ban on mechanised fishing.

neb6b41bd9a8.s: The Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to how many nautical miles from the baseline?
neb6b41bd9a8.x: The EEZ extends to 200 nautical miles, where the coastal state has sovereign rights over living and non-living resources.

n4469c4b5113.s: The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (2020) comes under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
n4469c4b5113.x: PMMSY, the Blue Revolution flagship, is under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying; the Ministry of Earth Sciences runs the Deep Ocean Mission.

n8a25d0998b7.s: Seabed deposits carrying copper, zinc, lead and iron along with silver, gold and platinum are called:
n8a25d0998b7.x: Polymetallic sulphides carry copper, zinc, lead, iron, silver, gold and platinum; polymetallic nodules contain nickel, copper, cobalt and manganese.

n422c5dccee5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2015 amendment to the MMDR Act?
o: It made auction mandatory for the grant of mineral concessions.
It created the National Mineral Exploration Trust.
It funded the District Mineral Foundation entirely from the Consolidated Fund of India.
Under it, the District Mineral Foundation gets miners' contributions linked to royalty.
n422c5dccee5.x: The DMF is funded by miners' contributions linked to royalty, not by the Consolidated Fund of India; auction and the NMET were indeed introduced in 2015.

n2f487b74d74.s: In Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL (2024), the Supreme Court held that States can tax mineral rights under which entry of the State List?
n2f487b74d74.x: The nine-judge bench held that States can tax mineral rights under Entry 50 and mineral land under Entry 49, and that royalty is not a tax.

ne9357b2592c.s: Which region of India is known as its mineral heartland?
ne9357b2592c.x: The Peninsular plateau is the mineral heartland; the Indo-Gangetic plains are known for alluvium and groundwater, the Himalaya/NE for forests and hydropower, and the Thar for scarce water.

n4f7c43ab943.s: Under PMKSY, the Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) is meant for:
o: Faster completion of major and medium irrigation projects
Repair, renovation and restoration of water bodies
n4f7c43ab943.x: AIBP is for faster completion of major and medium irrigation projects; command area development and RRR of water bodies fall under Har Khet Ko Pani.

nindian-geography-11-1.s: The Indira Gandhi Canal takes Sutlej-Beas water to western Rajasthan from which barrage?
nindian-geography-11-1.x: The Indira Gandhi Canal starts at the Harike Barrage in Punjab; Bhimgoda, Narora and Banbasa are the heads of the Upper Ganga, Lower Ganga and Sharda canals.

nb16c8933c94.s: The Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) was formed by merging all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Command Area Development and Water Management
nb16c8933c94.x: IWMP merged DPAP, DDP and IWDP; Command Area Development and Water Management is a component of PMKSY.

nda6648c63f4.s: India accounts for about what share of global groundwater extraction?
nda6648c63f4.x: India is the world's largest groundwater user, accounting for about a quarter of global extraction.

nd42a05dd6b8.s: The Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) is run by which department?
o: Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
nd42a05dd6b8.x: IWMP is run by the Department of Land Resources (DoLR) and aims at agricultural productivity and water conservation on degraded and rainfed land.

n5131985e703.s: Which body handles groundwater in India's water governance?
n5131985e703.x: The CGWB handles groundwater, while the CWC handles surface-water planning and flood control; CWPRS Pune is a hydraulic research institute.

n36440353ec7.s: The Atal Bhujal Yojana is the first Centrally Sponsored Scheme focused on:
o: Sewage treatment along the Ganga main stem
n36440353ec7.x: Atal Bhujal is the first community-led CSS on demand-side groundwater management; Ganga sewage treatment belongs to Namami Gange.

nae1e415eeb4.s: In the nine-fold land-use classification, land left uncultivated for more than 5 years is called:
nae1e415eeb4.x: Culturable wasteland has been uncultivated for over 5 years; other fallow is 1-5 years and current fallow up to 1 year.

nf6e50194580.s: Raising and tending forest trees, including regeneration, thinning and rotation, is called:
nf6e50194580.x: Silviculture is raising and tending forest trees; agroforestry is growing trees with crops or livestock on the same land.

n35582365a29.s: Kiruna and Gallivare in Swedish Lapland are known for:
n35582365a29.x: Kiruna and Gallivare are known for magnetite iron ore, not gold; they are in Swedish Lapland, not South Africa.

n3ed201e3828.s: Which country is the world's largest producer of nickel?
n3ed201e3828.x: Indonesia produces over half of the world's mined nickel; the DRC dominates cobalt and South Africa leads in manganese.

na1c06d5a7c8.s: Which agency implements India's Interlinking of Rivers programme?
na1c06d5a7c8.x: The NWDA implements the National Perspective Plan for interlinking, whose flagship link is Ken-Betwa.

n1b42ec72d15.s: Arabari, the forerunner of Joint Forest Management (1972), is in which State?
n1b42ec72d15.x: Arabari (1972) is in West Bengal; Appiko began in Karnataka's Salkani forest and Chipko in the Himalayas.

n215cfb9dd93.s: The Brundtland Commission report 'Our Common Future', which defined sustainable development, was published in:
n215cfb9dd93.x: 'Our Common Future' was published in 1987; 1972 is the year of the Club of Rome's 'Limits to Growth'.

nindian-geography-10-6.s: The Krishna Sagar dam in Karnataka is on which river?
nindian-geography-10-6.x: Krishna Sagar is on the Cauvery in Karnataka, as is Mettur in Tamil Nadu; Sardar Sarovar and Omkareshwar are on the Narmada.

n3f4c97905a8.s: The blue colour of sapphire is produced by:
n3f4c97905a8.x: Iron and titanium give sapphire (a corundum) its blue colour; chromium gives ruby its red, and chromium or vanadium gives emerald its green.

n25f28816c3c.x: Minerals are abiotic, not biotic; fossil fuels are non-renewable, while forests and fish are renewable.

n8c60f37e12d.s: Brick production is chiefly linked to the depletion of:
n8c60f37e12d.x: Brick production removes topsoil; deep bore tubewells deplete groundwater and agricultural expansion destroys biodiversity habitats.

n4153771cb9a.s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1988, the target of two-thirds area under forest applies to:
n4153771cb9a.x: Two-thirds is the forest target for the hills, not for the whole country; NFP 1988 also formally introduced JFM.

nworld-geography-4-4.x: Bolivia, Argentina and Chile together form the Lithium Triangle.

n6ea3e1bfa8d.s: The Gandikota reservoir, serving drought-prone Rayalaseema, is on which river?
n6ea3e1bfa8d.x: Gandikota reservoir is on the Pennar and is associated with the Telugu Ganga system serving Rayalaseema.

nindian-geography-11-3.s: The Buckingham Canal, a coastal backwater canal of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, runs along which coast?
nindian-geography-11-3.x: The Buckingham Canal lies along the Coromandel Coast in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, which makes it a coastal backwater canal.

n6244af07486.s: After ten years, PMKSY interventions had created or restored about how much irrigation potential?
n6244af07486.x: PMKSY created or restored 24.61 million hectares of irrigation potential and benefited about 27 million farmers.

nd26df3efd85.s: Shifting cultivation in the north-eastern hills is known as:
nd26df3efd85.x: Shifting cultivation in the NE hills is jhum; shorter fallow cycles degrade forests and increase soil erosion.

n914a114f232.s: Commercial gold mining in Andhra Pradesh began at ____ in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.
n914a114f232.x: Commercial gold mining in AP began at Jonnagiri, in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district.

na720da4bec1.s: Under the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, States may tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands:
o: Only within limits prescribed by the Centre
na720da4bec1.x: The 2026 amendment bars States from taxing mineral rights or mineral-bearing lands except within limits prescribed by the Centre.

nd1f236fd9d3.s: India's per-capita water availability, over 5,000 m³ at Independence, is now about:
nd1f236fd9d3.x: Per-capita water availability has declined from more than 5,000 m³ at Independence to about 1,400 m³ now.

n0e9fe556f6a.s: The Godavari-Krishna river transfer in Andhra Pradesh is associated with:
n0e9fe556f6a.x: The Godavari-Krishna transfer is associated with Pattiseema; Kurnool-Cuddapah is a canal project.

n09143fb21d4.s: A resource that exists but cannot be used at present because suitable technology is unavailable is called a:
n09143fb21d4.x: A stock exists but lacks the technology for its use; hydrogen from water is an example.

n3d323728087.s: The Bhakra-Nangal project, benefiting Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh, is on which river?
n3d323728087.x: Bhakra-Nangal is on the Sutlej; Gandhi Sagar is on the Chambal and Indira Sagar on the Narmada.

nb6f0e51b963.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Colorado Plateau – Cut by the Grand Canyon
Bolivian Altiplano – Intermontane plateau within the Andes
Mongolian Plateau – Intermontane plateau within the Andes
nb6f0e51b963.x: The Mongolian Plateau is an intermontane plateau of Central Asia; the plateau within the Andes is the Bolivian Altiplano.

ngeneral-geography-5-66.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Tibetan Plateau – About 2.5 million sq km
ngeneral-geography-5-66.x: The Columbia Plateau is a lava plateau of the north-western USA; the Meseta is the plateau of the Iberian Peninsula.

nea39522fcd4.s:
Assertion (A): The Thar Desert extends through India and Pakistan.
Reason (R): The Great Victoria is the largest desert in Australia.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nea39522fcd4.x: Both statements are true, but the size of Australia's Great Victoria Desert has nothing to do with the Thar's extent.

n0c5a5710c2d.s: Which river is confirmed as Earth's oldest continuously flowing river, about 300-400 million years old?
n0c5a5710c2d.x: The Finke (Larapinta) of central Australia, draining to the Lake Eyre Basin, is the oldest continuously flowing river.

nca3dfa939e4.s: The Drakensberg range is shared by South Africa and:
nca3dfa939e4.x: The Drakensberg is shared by South Africa and Lesotho.

n52600c0aae9.s: Which of the following is a young (Alpine) fold mountain range?
n52600c0aae9.x: The Atlas, like the Himalayas, are young Alpine fold mountains; the Appalachians and Urals are old.

ngeneral-geography-5-57.s: The Tibetan Plateau is an example of a(n):
ngeneral-geography-5-57.x: Tibet is an intermontane plateau; Africa is a continental plateau and the Columbia a lava plateau.

n11c02379378.s: The highest point of the Aravalli Range is:
n11c02379378.x: Gurushikhar (1,722 m) is the highest point of the Aravallis, India's oldest mountain system.

n85c0bcf17f7.s: The East African Plateau extends through:
n85c0bcf17f7.x: The East African Plateau covers Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

n0f9cdd8b7a7.s: The highest peak of Antarctica is:
n0f9cdd8b7a7.x: Vinson Massif is Antarctica's highest peak; Denali, Elbrus and Kilimanjaro top North America, Europe and Africa.

naafd8c333c3.s: Which is the youngest physiographic division of India?
naafd8c333c3.x: The Indo-Gangetic Plain, an aggradational plain over 2,400 km long, is India's youngest physiographic division, not the oldest.

nc804c36b07e.s: The Taklamakan Desert of Xinjiang lies in which basin?
nc804c36b07e.x: The Taklamakan lies in Xinjiang's Tarim basin and, like the Gobi, is a cold continental desert.

n8b83daba3c8.x: Plains generally lie below 200 metres; many are formed by rivers and are densely populated.

n896ee790d3b.s: The Andes extend along which side of South America?
n896ee790d3b.x: The Andes run along the Pacific side of South America.

nworld-geography-12-10.s: Which of the following is NOT a major mountain range of North America?
nworld-geography-12-10.x: The Andes are in South America; the Alaska Range, Appalachians and Sierra Nevada are in North America.

ngeneral-geography-5-64.s: The Panna, Bhander, Rewa and Rohtas plateaus of the Vindhyan region are:
ngeneral-geography-5-64.x: Panna, Bhander, Rewa and Rohtas are all fluvial plateaus of the Vindhyan region.

n850748c7d41.s: Which country is the third largest in the world by area?
n850748c7d41.x: The order is Russia, Canada, USA, China, Brazil, Australia and India, so the USA is third.

nworld-geography-20-8.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Channel Tunnel – Runs underneath the Strait of Gibraltar
English Channel – Separates the United Kingdom from France
Strait of Dover – Narrowest part of the English Channel
Strait of Gibraltar – Connects the Atlantic with the Mediterranean
nworld-geography-20-8.x: The Channel Tunnel runs beneath the English Channel, not the Strait of Gibraltar.

nworld-geography-22-4.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Lake Baikal – Deepest and largest freshwater lake by volume
Lake Tanganyika – Longest and second deepest freshwater lake
Lake Titicaca – Highest navigable lake in the world
Aral Sea – Highest navigable lake in the world
nworld-geography-22-4.x: The Aral Sea is famous for shrinking due to irrigation diversion; the highest navigable lake is Titicaca.

nworld-geography-22-8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Lake Baikal is the oldest freshwater lake.
The Baikal seal is associated with Lake Baikal.
Lake Victoria is also known as Lake Nyasa.
Lake Victoria is the largest tropical lake.
nworld-geography-22-8.x: Lake Nyasa is the other name of Lake Malawi, not Lake Victoria.

nworld-geography-20-6.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: English Channel – Between the Atlantic Ocean and the North Sea
Bass Strait – Between Australia and New Zealand
Mozambique Channel – Between Mozambique and Madagascar
Dardanelles – Between the Sea of Marmara and the Aegean Sea
nworld-geography-20-6.x: Bass Strait lies between Australia and Tasmania.

na3e32ad569a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about straits?
o: The Strait of Gibraltar lies between Spain and Morocco.
The Bering Strait connects the Arctic Ocean with the Atlantic Ocean.
The Kerch Strait connects the Black Sea with the Sea of Azov.
The Bering Strait lies between Russia and the USA.
na3e32ad569a.x: The Bering Strait connects the Arctic with the Pacific, not the Atlantic.

nworld-geography-8-8.s: Which river forms an inland delta in Mali?
nworld-geography-8-8.x: The Niger forms an inland delta in Mali; the Congo is also called the Zaire.

n9c5525bdebc.s: The world's highest waterfall, about 979 m, is:
n9c5525bdebc.x: Angel Falls (Venezuela) is the highest at about 979 m; Tugela is second highest, Victoria the largest sheet of falling water and Iguazu the largest fall system.

nworld-geography-23-16.s: The smallest of Japan's four main islands is:
nworld-geography-23-16.x: Shikoku is the smallest; Hokkaido is the northernmost and Kyushu the southernmost.

nworld-geography-23-13.x: The Aleutian Islands lie between Alaska and Russia.

n7d7fa704c0a.s: The largest freshwater lake in the world by area is:
n7d7fa704c0a.x: Lake Superior (USA-Canada) is the largest freshwater lake by area; Baikal is largest by volume and the Caspian, though the largest lake, is saline.

nworld-geography-13-2.s: The shallowest sea in the world is:
nworld-geography-13-2.x: The Sea of Azov is the shallowest sea; the Sargasso Sea has no land boundary.

nworld-geography-22-12.s: Which lake lies wholly within Kazakhstan?
nworld-geography-22-12.x: Lake Balkhash lies wholly within Kazakhstan, while the Aral Sea is shared by Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

n45135305a00.s: Which is the only Great Lake lying wholly in the USA?
n45135305a00.x: Only Lake Michigan lies wholly in the USA; Ontario is the smallest Great Lake, drained by the St Lawrence.

nda7d5b53b7e.s: Lake Malawi lies at the ____ end of the Great Rift Valley lake chain.
nda7d5b53b7e.x: Lake Malawi is at the southern end of the chain; Tanganyika, Albert, Edward and Kivu lie in the western (Albertine) branch.

nworld-geography-7-8.s: Which river crosses the Equator twice?
nworld-geography-7-8.x: The Congo crosses the Equator twice; the Amazon has the largest drainage basin and the Yangtze is Asia's longest river.

nworld-geography-13-10.s: Eritrea lies on the coast of which sea?
nworld-geography-13-10.x: Eritrea is on the Red Sea; Turkmenistan is on the Caspian, Georgia on the Black Sea and Lebanon on the Mediterranean.

nworld-geography-23-4.s: Baffin Island belongs to which country?
nworld-geography-23-4.x: Baffin Island is in Arctic Canada.

n74922912c99.s: The Kiel Canal, linking the North Sea with the Baltic Sea, lies in:
n74922912c99.x: The Kiel Canal is in Germany, not Denmark.

nindian-geography-15-4.s: The Tyrrhenian Sea lies to the west of:
nindian-geography-15-4.x: The Tyrrhenian Sea lies west of Italy.

nc51cd13c8a6.s: Lake Ontario is connected to Lake Erie by which canal, bypassing Niagara Falls?
nc51cd13c8a6.x: The Welland Canal links Erie and Ontario and bypasses Niagara Falls.

n6395af1030c.x: The Mississippi rises at Lake Itasca in Minnesota and flows north to south into the Gulf of Mexico.

nindian-geography-37-9.s: Which Indian lake was formed in a meteorite crater?
nindian-geography-37-9.x: Lonar is a meteorite crater lake; Loktak has phumdis, Roopkund is the skeleton lake and Ghepan is glacial.

na100b2a780f.s: The world's largest desert lake is:
na100b2a780f.x: Lake Turkana in Kenya's Eastern Rift is the largest desert lake; Lake Van is the largest alkaline lake.

nworld-geography-7-4.s: The deepest river in the world is:
nworld-geography-7-4.x: The Congo is the deepest river; the Nile is the longest and the Amazon the largest by discharge.

nworld-geography-7-14.s: The Kariba Dam is on which river?
nworld-geography-7-14.x: Kariba Dam is on the Zambezi; Hoover Dam is on the Colorado.

n0afc81a18ef.s: Niagara Falls lies between which two lakes?
n0afc81a18ef.x: Niagara Falls lies between Lakes Erie and Ontario.

n3d45921733e.s: The Danube, which rises in the Black Forest, drains into:
n3d45921733e.x: The Danube drains into the Black Sea; the Rhine and Elbe reach the North Sea.

n4919f97eb36.x: The Blue Nile rises from Lake Tana in Ethiopia; the Nile empties into the Mediterranean.

n063cfda0180.s: Which is the second largest island in the world?
n063cfda0180.x: The order is Greenland, New Guinea, Borneo, Madagascar, so New Guinea is second.

n27e79cf768d.s: The Amazon, rising in the Andes of Peru, drains into the:
n27e79cf768d.x: The Amazon flows through Peru, Colombia and Brazil into the Atlantic, not the Pacific.

nc7b440cfcbf.s: Which of the following countries does NOT border the Black Sea?
nc7b440cfcbf.x: The Black Sea is bordered by Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia; Iran borders the Caspian.

nad3f7aa2ee4.s: The Mekong does NOT flow through which country?
nad3f7aa2ee4.x: The Mekong flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam, not Malaysia.

nworld-geography-14-5.s: Which of the following is a doubly landlocked country?

nworld-geography-7-5.s: The Tigris and Euphrates meet to form the ____ before draining into the Persian Gulf.
nworld-geography-7-5.x: The Tigris and Euphrates join as the Shatt al-Arab, which drains into the Persian Gulf.

nworld-geography-23-5.s: The most populous island of Indonesia is:
nworld-geography-23-5.x: Java is Indonesia's most populous island.

nworld-geography-20-16.s: The stormiest and widest passage in the world is the:
nworld-geography-20-16.x: The Drake Passage is both the stormiest and the widest passage.

nworld-geography-8-18.s: The most international river, flowing through 10 countries, is the:
nworld-geography-8-18.x: The Danube flows through 10 countries and is the most international river.

nworld-geography-22-7.s: The maximum depth of Lake Baikal is about:
nworld-geography-22-7.x: Lake Baikal in Siberia is 1,642 m deep and holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh water.

nworld-geography-8-13.s: The Three Gorges Dam, the world's largest hydroelectric project, is on which river?
nworld-geography-8-13.x: The Three Gorges Dam is on the Yangtze, Asia's longest river.

nworld-geography-7-6.s: Which river is known as the 'Oil River' of West Africa?
nworld-geography-7-6.x: The Niger is called the Oil River of West Africa.

nindian-geography-15-9.s: The Mediterranean Sea is connected to the Atlantic Ocean through the:
nindian-geography-15-9.x: The Mediterranean joins the Atlantic at Gibraltar; the Black Sea reaches it through the Turkish Straits and the Mediterranean.

nworld-geography-8-7.s: Which country is known as the 'Gift of the Nile'?
nworld-geography-8-7.x: Egypt is called the Gift of the Nile; the Nile basin has 11 countries.

nworld-geography-14-6.s: Norway's deeply indented coastline is known for its thousands of:
nworld-geography-14-6.x: Norway's coast is deeply indented with thousands of fjords and islands.

nworld-geography-7-17.s: Spring floods on the Ob, Yenisei and Lena occur mainly because:
o: Their mouths thaw while the upper reaches stay frozen
Their upper reaches thaw while the Arctic mouths stay frozen
They flow southward into warmer regions
Glaciers in their basins burst in spring
nworld-geography-7-17.x: These rivers flow north, so their upper reaches thaw first while their Arctic mouths stay frozen; the ice blocks the water and causes floods.

nworld-geography-20-4.s: The Strait of Magellan offers a sheltered alternative route to the:
nworld-geography-20-4.x: The Strait of Magellan is a sheltered route used instead of the Drake Passage.

nworld-geography-14-3.s: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
nworld-geography-14-3.x: Canada's vast Arctic Archipelago and coasts on three oceans give it the longest coastline.

nindian-geography-37-6.s: Floating phumdis are associated with which lake?
nindian-geography-37-6.x: Loktak is known for phumdis; Wular is the largest freshwater lake by volume.

nindian-geography-37-15.s: Which of the following is an artificial lake?
nindian-geography-37-15.x: Kodaikanal Lake is artificial; Vembanad is Kerala's great kayal.

nworld-geography-13-19.s: Of the Mediterranean, Black, Caspian and Aral Seas, which lies farthest east?
nworld-geography-13-19.x: From west to east they lie Mediterranean, Black Sea, Caspian, Aral, so the Aral is easternmost.

n65e0acea19f.s: The Bosphorus connects the Black Sea with the:
n65e0acea19f.x: The Bosphorus links the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara; the Dardanelles links the Aegean and the Marmara.

nindian-geography-15-12.s: Which of the following countries does NOT border the Caspian Sea?
nindian-geography-15-12.x: The Caspian is bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan; Uzbekistan does not touch it.

n2ab5d3ad51c.s: Iran is not a party to UNCLOS, yet transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz binds it as:
n2ab5d3ad51c.x: Though Iran is not party to UNCLOS, the transit passage principle is binding as customary international law.

n04771a98193.s: Pulicat Lagoon, India's second largest brackish lagoon, is separated from the sea by:
n04771a98193.x: Pulicat, in Tirupati district, is separated from the sea by Sriharikota; it is second only to Chilika.

nc46c7adb35d.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates given)
nc46c7adb35d.s: The Durand Line was the boundary between British India and:
nc46c7adb35d.x: The Durand Line was the British India-Afghanistan boundary; the McMahon Line concerns India-China east of Nepal.

ne42a3589453.s: Which water body lies to the south-west of India?
ne42a3589453.x: The Lakshadweep Sea lies to the south-west, with the Arabian Sea to the west, the Bay of Bengal to the east and the Indian Ocean to the south.

nindian-geography-6-4.s: Which neighbouring country borders Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram?
nindian-geography-6-4.x: Myanmar borders Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram.

naa4fd3eb1f1.s: The 1949 ceasefire line in Jammu and Kashmir was renamed the Line of Control under the:
naa4fd3eb1f1.x: The LoC began as the 1949 ceasefire line and was renamed under the Simla Agreement of 1972.

nindian-geography-25-17.s: The Strait of Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the:
nindian-geography-25-17.x: Hormuz links the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

nindian-geography-5-6.s: Which Indian State borders China, Nepal and Bhutan?
nindian-geography-5-6.x: Sikkim borders China, Nepal and Bhutan; Uttarakhand borders China and Nepal, and Arunachal China, Bhutan and Myanmar.

nindian-geography-15-6.s: The Laccadive Sea lies to the ____ of India.
nindian-geography-15-6.x: The Laccadive Sea lies south-west of India; the Arabian Sea is west and the Bay of Bengal east.

n251688f8a87.s: Which country does NOT share a maritime border with the Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
n251688f8a87.x: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands share maritime borders with Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia, not Sri Lanka.

n8e166039f0d.s: Andhra Pradesh (about 1,62,970 sq km) ranks ____ among Indian States in area.
n8e166039f0d.x: Andhra Pradesh, about 4.96% of India's area, ranks seventh by area.

o: Minicoy and the main Lakshadweep group
n88c502e40e5.x: The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives; the Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the main Lakshadweep group.

n671f10e5661.s: Under which line, followed by India, is Aksai Chin shown as Indian territory?
n671f10e5661.x: India follows the Johnson Line for Aksai Chin; China follows the McDonald Line.

nindian-geography-25-16.s: The Strait of Malacca lies between:
nindian-geography-25-16.x: Malacca lies between Indonesia and Malaysia; the Palk Strait separates India and Sri Lanka.

nbe79ac18a9d.s: India shares its longest land border with:
nbe79ac18a9d.x: Bangladesh (4,096.7 km) is India's longest land border; China (3,488 km) is second.

n4415849ca8b.s: Yanam, a part of Puducherry, lies within which State?
n4415849ca8b.x: Yanam lies in the Godavari delta of Andhra Pradesh; Mahe is in Kerala, and Puducherry and Karaikal are in Tamil Nadu.

nindian-geography-6-6.s: Afghanistan lies to the ____ of India.
nindian-geography-6-6.x: Afghanistan lies north-west of India; Nepal is north, Pakistan west and Bangladesh east.

nworld-geography-20-9.s: The world's busiest commercial strait, between Malaysia and Sumatra, is the:
nworld-geography-20-9.x: The Strait of Malacca, between Malaysia and Sumatra, is the busiest commercial strait.

nindian-geography-25-15.s: The Strait of Dover joins the English Channel with the:
nindian-geography-25-15.x: The Strait of Dover links the English Channel and the North Sea.

nindian-geography-5-14.s: Which of the following is part of the Purvanchal (Eastern Hills)?
nindian-geography-5-14.x: The Purvanchal includes the Patkai Bum, the Naga Hills and the Arakan Yoma continuation.

nindian-geography-6-5.s: Nagaland shares an international border with:

nindian-geography-5-12.s: The Line of Actual Control, a de facto boundary from the post-1962 period, separates India from:
nindian-geography-5-12.x: The LAC is the de facto line between India and China.

nindian-geography-5-15.s: Which State has India's longest boundary with Myanmar?
nindian-geography-5-15.x: Arunachal Pradesh has the longest border with Myanmar; Mizoram borders both Bangladesh and Myanmar.

nindian-geography-5-9.s: West Bengal shares international borders with Nepal, Bhutan and:
nindian-geography-5-9.x: West Bengal borders Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh.

nafd5b8d1db3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the parallel ranges of the Himalayas?
o: The Karakoram is part of the Trans-Himalaya.
The Ladakh Range continues eastwards into Tibet as the Zaskar Range.
The Zaskar Range lies south of the Karakoram.
The Kashmir Valley separates the Zaskar from the Pir Panjal.
nafd5b8d1db3.x: The Ladakh Range continues into Tibet as the Kailash Range, not the Zaskar; the other three statements are correct.

n054e878626d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the dimensions of the Himalayas?
o: They cover an area of about 15 lakh sq km.
They extend about 2,414 km from Nanga Parbat to Namcha Barwa.
They are about 500 km wide in Kashmir.
They narrow to about 200 km in Arunachal Pradesh.
n054e878626d.x: The Himalayas cover about 5 lakh sq km, not 15 lakh sq km.

n8266272b146.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Himalayan ranges?
o: The Himadri is the loftiest and oldest range, with a granite core.
The Shiwalik is the youngest and narrowest range.
The Shiwalik is the northernmost of the three parallel ranges.
The Shiwalik averages about 1,300 m in height.
n8266272b146.x: The Himadri is the northernmost of the three; the Shiwalik is the outermost (southernmost) range.

nafe61c5fc0f.s:
Assertion (A): The Himalayas were uplifted from Tethys sediments during the Tertiary (Eocene to Pliocene).
Reason (R): The Indian plate collided with the Eurasian plate about 4-5 crore years ago.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nafe61c5fc0f.x: Both are true: the India-Eurasia collision about 4-5 crore years ago uplifted the Tethys sediments into the Himalayas, which are still rising.

n2afa903e867.s: The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills lie in which State?
n2afa903e867.x: The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills form the Shillong Plateau in Meghalaya; Mizoram has the Mizo (Lushai) hills.

n0ba424c6e2d.s: The Siachen Glacier, in the Nubra region, lies in which range?
n0ba424c6e2d.x: Siachen lies in the Karakoram and marks Ladakh's northern limit.

n6ecf0e62d62.s: Nanda Devi belongs to which Himalayan range?
n6ecf0e62d62.x: Nanda Devi belongs to the Greater Himalaya (Himadri), not the Middle Himalaya as some notes wrongly place it.

nf16c239118f.s: Debris from which Himalayan system helped build the Indo-Gangetic Plain?
nf16c239118f.x: Debris through the Shiwalik system helped form the Indo-Gangetic Plain.

n72fdf15eb59.s: The steep slope of the Himalayas faces:
n72fdf15eb59.x: The Himadri has asymmetrical folds: the steep slope faces the plains and the gentler slope faces Tibet.

nworld-geography-12-5.s: K2 (8,611 m) lies in which mountain range?
nworld-geography-12-5.x: K2 is in the Karakoram on the Pakistan-China border.

nindian-geography-14-11.s: The Arakan Yoma is located in:
nindian-geography-14-11.x: The Arakan Yoma is in western Myanmar; the Chin Range reaches Manipur.

nindian-geography-13-4.s: Thalghat and Bhor Ghat are located in:
nindian-geography-13-4.x: Thalghat and Bhor Ghat are in Maharashtra; the Palghat Gap is in Kerala.

nindian-geography-13-14.s: Diphu La and Pangsau passes lie on India's border with:
nindian-geography-13-14.x: Both Diphu La and Pangsau are on the India-Myanmar border.

nindian-geography-13-19.x: The Brahmaputra enters India near Yang Yap in Arunachal Pradesh.

nd0b650a2624.s: In the standard (Burrard) division, the Kumaon Himalaya lies between which rivers?
nd0b650a2624.x: The Kumaon Himalaya lies between the Sutlej and Kali; Punjab is Indus-Sutlej, Nepal is Kali-Teesta and Assam is Teesta-Dihang.

nindian-geography-12-5.s: Which of the following Himalayan peaks lies farthest east?
nindian-geography-12-5.x: From east to west the order is Namcha Barwa, Kanchenjunga, Everest and Nanda Devi.

nbaaaccc8d74.s: Which of the following Purvanchal hill groups runs north-south?
nbaaaccc8d74.x: The Garo-Khasi-Jaintia and Naga hills run east-west, joining the north-south Mizo and Rakhine hills.

n4eaf0c8238a.s: Which of the following ranges belongs to the Himachal (Lesser) Himalaya?
n4eaf0c8238a.x: The Pir Panjal is a major Lesser Himalayan range, about 300 km long in the Jhelum-Beas sector.

n8c0f7597570.s: Which is regarded as the highest plateau in India?
n8c0f7597570.x: The Ladakh Plateau of the Trans-Himalaya, which formed before the Himalayas, is the highest plateau in India.

nf4698b1df6d.s: After the knee-bend near Namcha Barwa and the Dihang gorge, the Himalayas turn south as the:
nf4698b1df6d.x: Beyond the Dihang gorge the Himalayas turn south as the Purvanchal hills, generally 500-3,000 m high.

n7ac24c44b50.s: The highest peak lying wholly within India is:
n7ac24c44b50.x: Kanchenjunga is India's highest peak but lies on the India-Nepal boundary; the highest wholly in India is Nanda Devi.

n6d30f4a5496.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's coastal plains?
o: The western coast is generally drier than the eastern coast.
The western coast is generally narrow and submergent.
The eastern coast is generally broad and emergent.
Estuaries mark the western coast, while large deltas mark the eastern coast.
n6d30f4a5496.x: The western coast is generally wetter; the eastern coast is comparatively dry.

n244debf513d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Peninsular Plateau?
o: It is the largest and oldest physiographic division.
It tilts towards the west, so most rivers flow westward.
It is a Precambrian Gondwana shield.
It is a triangular block of igneous and metamorphic rocks.
n244debf513d.x: The Peninsular Plateau tilts eastward, so most of its rivers flow east.

nd7c4627f2e2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Nallamala is associated with the Chenchus.
Papikondalu holds the Srisailam Tiger Reserve.
Seshachalam is associated with Red Sanders.
nd7c4627f2e2.x: The Srisailam Tiger Reserve is in the Nallamala; Papikondalu is associated with a National Park.

nd6575441bbe.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Shipki La – Where the Sutlej enters India
nd6575441bbe.x: Zoji La is in the Zaskar range on the Srinagar-Leh route; Lipulekh is the Pithoragarh pass.

ncd14a1368e1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Chilika is a lagoon lake in Odisha.
Kolleru continues to be a coastal lagoon separated from the sea.
Pulicat is the second-largest brackish lagoon.
Kolleru is a freshwater lake between the Krishna and Godavari.
ncd14a1368e1.x: Kolleru was formerly a lagoon but became an inland freshwater lake due to coastal emergence.

nindian-geography-40-11.s:
Assertion (A): Dandakaranya covers about 89,078 sq km.
Reason (R): The Malwa Plateau lies in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nindian-geography-40-11.x: Both are true, but the location of the Malwa Plateau has nothing to do with the extent of Dandakaranya.

n5e38974b467.s: The Border Roads Organisation is building a 120 km all-weather road to which pass?
n5e38974b467.x: The BRO is building a 120 km road to Lipulekh; Shipki La was opened to Indian tourists for border tourism.

n5c1cb537653.s: The longitudinal valleys of the Shiwaliks are called:
n5c1cb537653.x: The Shiwaliks, the youngest and narrowest range, have longitudinal valleys called duns.

n4f4b810c6c6.s: The Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is a seasonal:
n4f4b810c6c6.x: The Rann is a seasonal salt marsh (Great Rann to the north, Little Rann to the south); it was a lowland, not a high mountainous tract.

ngeneral-geography-5-18.s: Which plateau is mineral-rich and drained by the Damodar?
ngeneral-geography-5-18.x: Chotanagpur is mineral-rich and drained by the Damodar; Malwa lies between the Aravalli and Vindhya.

n005bcf537ac.s: The Vindhyas lie to the ____ of the Malwa Plateau.
n005bcf537ac.x: The Vindhyas lie south of the Malwa Plateau; the Malwa is not south of the Vindhyas.

n732b4c3f1e9.s: In the Northern Plains, the marshy belt where Bhabar streams re-emerge is the:
n732b4c3f1e9.x: Terai is the marshy, forested belt where Bhabar streams re-emerge; kankar-bearing older alluvium is the Bhangar.

nc32a330b716.s: The Eastern Ghats extend for about 1,750 km between which rivers?
nc32a330b716.x: The discontinuous Eastern Ghats run about 1,750 km from the Mahanadi to the Vaigai.

na1412104a48.s: The Eastern and Western Ghats meet at the:
na1412104a48.x: The Nilgiri Hills form the southern point where the Eastern and Western Ghats meet.

nf0598f42a9d.s: The Tropic of Cancer crosses how many States of India?
nf0598f42a9d.x: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight States; the Standard Meridian 82°30' E passes through Mirzapur.

nindian-geography-28-12.x: The Maikal Range rises at Amarkantak on the MP-Chhattisgarh border; Pachmarhi is in the Mahadeo Range.

nb0548303820.s: India's only active volcano is on:
nb0548303820.x: Barren Island is India's only active volcano (last erupted 2017); Narcondam is dormant.

n04455153ab4.s: The Central Highlands of the Peninsular Plateau lie north of which river?
n04455153ab4.x: The Central Highlands lie north of the Narmada and include the Aravalli, Malwa and Vindhya regions.

n22bb1a3c121.s: Dandakaranya is a highland of which part of the Peninsula?
n22bb1a3c121.x: Dandakaranya (about 89,078 sq km) is a central-eastern Peninsular highland.

nindian-geography-32-18.s: Divi Island lies among the distributaries of which river?
nindian-geography-32-18.x: Divi lies among the Krishna distributaries; Sriharikota separates Pulicat from the Bay of Bengal.

n756e54ff845.s: Plains formed by wind-blown silt, as in China, are called:
n756e54ff845.x: Loess plains come from wind-blown silt; outwash plains are glacial meltwater deposits.

n74b9a1b3fa6.s: The word 'trap' in Deccan Traps comes from a Swedish word meaning:
n74b9a1b3fa6.x: 'Trap' is Swedish for step; the Traps formed by fissure eruptions of basaltic lava.

n59ed3747f0d.x: Konkan is the Maharashtra-Goa coast; Kannad runs from Goa to Mangaluru and Malabar from Mangaluru to Kanyakumari.

nindian-geography-39-9.s: The Chota Nagpur Plateau lies mainly in:
nindian-geography-39-9.x: Chota Nagpur lies mainly in Jharkhand; Malwa is in MP and Rajasthan.

n6c733a0835b.s: The Satpura Range lies between the Narmada and the ____ valleys.
n6c733a0835b.x: The Satpura lies between the Narmada and Tapi valleys; the Vindhyas lie north of the Narmada.

nindian-geography-12-8.s: The Garhjat Hills are located in:
nindian-geography-12-8.x: The Garhjat Hills are in Odisha; the Shevaroys are in Salem and the Palnis in Dindigul.

nindian-geography-14-4.s: The Mandav Hills are located in:
nindian-geography-14-4.x: The Mandav Hills are in Gujarat; the Biligirirangans are in south-eastern Karnataka.

nindian-geography-32-17.s: Salsette Island, covering Mumbai and Thane, is in:
nindian-geography-32-17.x: Salsette is in Maharashtra (Mumbai-Thane); Minicoy is in Lakshadweep.

nindian-geography-14-7.s: The Seshachalam Hills are located in:
nindian-geography-14-7.x: The Seshachalam Hills are in southern Andhra Pradesh; the Satpuras are in central India.

n43b927394b5.s: The average height of the Eastern Ghats is about:
n43b927394b5.x: The Eastern Ghats, made of khondalite and charnockite, average about 610 m.

n4aede93db48.s: The southernmost island of Lakshadweep is:
n4aede93db48.x: Minicoy is the largest and southernmost island; the Amindivi group lies north of 11° N.

nindian-geography-14-14.s: Yercaud is located in which hills?
nindian-geography-14-14.x: Yercaud is in the Shevaroy Hills; Ooty is in the Nilgiris and Anaimudi tops the Anaimalai Range.

n58fb72755aa.s: The Meghalaya Plateau is a detached north-eastern extension of the:
n58fb72755aa.x: The Meghalaya Plateau, with the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia Hills, is a detached extension of the Peninsular Plateau.

n926af544806.s: The true desert in the western part of the Thar is called:
n926af544806.x: Marusthali (west) is the true desert; Bagar (east) is the semi-arid strip bordering the Aravallis.

nad5c783974c.s: The highest peak of the Satpura Range is:
nad5c783974c.x: Dhupgarh (1,350 m, Mahadeo hills) is the Satpura's highest peak; Amarkantak is in the Maikala range.

n4f9ac148940.s: The Pal Ghat gap lies between the Nilgiris and the:
n4f9ac148940.x: Pal Ghat lies between the Nilgiris and the Anaimalai hills, between Kerala and Tamil Nadu, about 24-30 km wide.

n55fd49ba6bb.s: The highest feature of the Kachchh-Kathiawar region, an extinct volcano, is:
n55fd49ba6bb.x: Girnar, an extinct volcano, is the highest point of the region; Kathiawar is part of the Peninsular Plateau.

nc500e2827b3.s: The largest kayal (backwater) of the Malabar coast is:
nc500e2827b3.x: Vembanad, on which Cochin port lies, is the largest kayal; Ashtamudi is another kayal.

ncffd3bd974d.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three official India-Tibet trade routes?
ncffd3bd974d.x: Shipki La, Nathu La and Lipulekh are the official trade routes; Bomdila is the gateway to Tawang.

nef00e60e910.s: The north-south extent of India's mainland is about:
nef00e60e910.x: India's mainland extends about 3,214 km north-south and 2,933 km east-west.

nc876b6a409a.s: The Eastern Ghats are cut through by all of the following rivers EXCEPT:
nc876b6a409a.x: The Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi cut through the Eastern Ghats; the Narmada does not.

n0fcbff36fb2.x: Kavaratti is the capital of Lakshadweep, a group of coral atolls and India's smallest UT (about 32 sq km).

nb38daf9758a.s: India covers about what share of the world's land area?
nb38daf9758a.x: India's 32,87,263 sq km is about 2.4% of the world's land, making it the seventh largest country.

n837d64d81f1.s: India's land frontier, touching seven countries, is about how long?
n837d64d81f1.x: India's land frontier is about 15,200 km (15,106.7 km in some sources); its longest border is with Bangladesh.

nindian-geography-44-9.s: Which of the following valleys is NOT in Himachal Pradesh?
nindian-geography-44-9.x: Lahaul, Parvati and Kullu are in Himachal Pradesh; Tura is in Meghalaya.

ndc8f083db74.s: India's relatively straight coastline is chiefly the result of:
ndc8f083db74.x: The straight coastline is due to faulting, not glacial deposition; the coasts separated from Gondwana in the Cretaceous-early Tertiary.

nindian-geography-28-20.s: Which of the following hills is NOT located in Karnataka?
nindian-geography-28-20.x: Biligiriranga, Nandi and Chamundi are in Karnataka; the Garo Hills are in Meghalaya.

ngeneral-geography-5-88.s: The Ganga-Brahmaputra Delta is an example of a:
ngeneral-geography-5-88.x: Deltaic plains form by deposition at river mouths, as in the Ganga-Brahmaputra Delta.

ngeneral-geography-5-13.s: The Peninsular Plateau of India is best described as:
ngeneral-geography-5-13.x: The Peninsular Plateau is an ancient stable crystalline landmass; the Northern Plains are alluvial and the Indian Desert is the arid west.

nindian-geography-40-12.s: The Ranchi Plateau is located in:
nindian-geography-40-12.x: The Ranchi Plateau is part of the Chota Nagpur region in Jharkhand, not Meghalaya.

nindian-geography-40-6.s: The mineral-rich Chota Nagpur Plateau lies mainly in:
nindian-geography-40-6.x: Most of the Chota Nagpur Plateau is in Jharkhand; it extends into Odisha, West Bengal, Bihar and Chhattisgarh.

nindian-geography-48-6.s: The Northern Circars coast extends from the Mahanadi to the:
nindian-geography-48-6.x: The Northern Circars run from the Mahanadi to the Krishna; the Coromandel Coast runs from the Krishna delta to Kanyakumari.

nindian-geography-40-18.s: Malnad (Malenadu), a mountainous and densely forested region, lies in:
nindian-geography-40-18.x: Malnad is the forested hilly west of Karnataka.

ngeneral-geography-5-4.s: The Deccan Plateau is predominantly ____ in origin.
ngeneral-geography-5-4.x: The Deccan Plateau is built mainly of basaltic lava.

nindian-geography-28-6.s: The highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills (Blue Mountains) is:
nindian-geography-28-6.x: Doddabetta (about 2,637 m) tops the Nilgiris; 2,695 m is Anaimudi.

ngeneral-geography-5-103.s: A salt marsh that floods in the monsoon and dries into a desert describes the:
ngeneral-geography-5-103.x: The Rann of Kutch is a salt marsh and a seasonal marshy desert.

n9ef8a4ff304.s: Which feature of the Indian Desert appears only with rainfall?
n9ef8a4ff304.x: Seasonal streams appear during rainfall; the desert otherwise has arid weather, sand dunes and thorny bushes.

nindian-geography-40-15.s: The Bhander Plateau forms the ____ part of the Vindhyan scarpland.
nindian-geography-40-15.x: The Bhander Plateau is in the Vindhyan region and forms the southern part of the scarpland, not the northern.

nindian-geography-32-12.x: Salsette is India's most populous island; Elephanta is about 10 km from the Gateway of India.

nindian-geography-44-19.s: The Narmada Valley lies between which ranges?
nindian-geography-44-19.x: The Narmada flows between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

nindian-geography-12-9.s: Which of the following is NOT located in Maharashtra?
nindian-geography-12-9.x: The Balaghat, Harishchandra and Satmala ranges are in Maharashtra; the Mandav Hills are in Gujarat.

n2c373881d13.s: The Deccan Traps originally covered about 10 lakh sq km; today they cover about:
n2c373881d13.x: They now cover about 5 lakh sq km, thinning from about 3,000 m in the west to about 150 m in the east.

n9fa1d9ba8d3.s: Under the revised measurement, Andhra Pradesh's coastline is about:
n9fa1d9ba8d3.x: The revised figure is 1,053.07 km, ranking AP third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; the earlier 974 km placed it second.

nbef44523865.s: Which is the northernmost of the major Himalayan structural zones?
nbef44523865.x: From north to south the zones are the Indus-Tsangpo Suture, Main Central Thrust, Main Boundary Thrust and Himalayan Frontal Fault.

n03e19f62ab5.s: Emergent coasts, with wide plains, bars, lagoons and deltas, result from:
n03e19f62ab5.x: Emergent coasts form when land rises or the sea falls, giving wide plains, bars, lagoons and deltas.

n0b7ecf3546c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the antecedent Himalayan rivers?
o: They existed before the Himalayan uplift.
They kept their courses by cutting deep gorges.
Entrenched meanders are not found along them.
Valley-in-valley topography and paired terraces mark them.
n0b7ecf3546c.x: Entrenched meanders are also a feature of antecedent rivers, so saying they are not found is wrong.

nindian-geography-1-23.s:
Assertion (A): The Sankosh marks the boundary between Assam and West Bengal.
Reason (R): The Sankosh rises in northern Bhutan and joins the Brahmaputra.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nindian-geography-1-23.x: Both are true, but where the Sankosh rises and which river it joins do not explain why it marks the Assam-West Bengal boundary.

nindian-geography-1-34.s: In Pakistan, the Kishanganga river is known as the:
nindian-geography-1-34.x: The Kishanganga is called the Neelum in Pakistan; the Jhelum rises at Verinag.

nindian-geography-31-5.s: The Rihand Project is located in:
nindian-geography-31-5.x: Rihand is in Uttar Pradesh; Hirakud is in Odisha and Damodar Valley serves Jharkhand and West Bengal.

nd82a0dbc22d.s: The Betwa joins the Yamuna at:
nd82a0dbc22d.x: The Betwa joins the Yamuna at Hamirpur; the Chambal joins in Etawah.

n652354e75b0.s: At Farakka, the left arm of the Ganga is the:
n652354e75b0.x: The left arm is the Bhagirathi-Hooghly; the right arm, the Padma, joins the Brahmaputra and Meghna.

nfa915209637.s: Which State has the highest number of polluted river stretches?
nfa915209637.x: Maharashtra has the most polluted river stretches (BOD above 3 mg/L).

n85fafb933db.s: About how much of the Brahmaputra's 2,900 km course lies in India?
n85fafb933db.x: Only about 885 km of the Brahmaputra's roughly 2,900 km course lies in India.

n6d752a2d76f.s: The Ganga is navigable up to:
n6d752a2d76f.x: The Ganga is navigable up to Prayagraj, not only up to Farakka.

nc7b7d48014b.s: The Teesta river rises at which lake in North Sikkim?
nc7b7d48014b.x: The Teesta (about 414 km) rises at Tso Lhamo Lake; the Rangeet is its largest tributary.

nindian-geography-1-12.s: The Rangeet is a tributary of the:
nindian-geography-1-12.x: The Rangeet joins the Teesta, not the Brahmaputra directly; the Manas and Kopili are direct Brahmaputra tributaries.

nindian-geography-1-17.x: The Ghaghra rises at Mapchachungo Glacier and meets the Ganga at Revilganj in Saran, Bihar.

nindian-geography-1-4.s: The Yamuna rises at the Yamunotri Glacier on the slopes of:
nindian-geography-1-4.x: The Yamuna rises at Yamunotri on the western slopes of Banderpunch Peak.

nindian-geography-31-8.s: The Srisailam Project is on which river?
nindian-geography-31-8.x: Srisailam is on the Krishna, not the Tungabhadra; Nagarjuna Sagar is also on the Krishna and Pochampad on the Godavari.

nindian-geography-2-9.x: The Damodar flows into the Hugli.

nindian-geography-1-5.s: The Brahmaputra is known as the Jamuna in:
nindian-geography-1-5.x: The Brahmaputra is the Tsangpo in Tibet, the Dihang in Arunachal and the Jamuna in Bangladesh.

nindian-geography-1-51.s: In Pakistan, the Ravi joins the:
nindian-geography-1-51.x: The Ravi joins the Chenab, which also takes the Jhelum, and the combined flow joins the Sutlej before the Indus.

nindian-geography-2-11.s: Which of the following joins the Yamuna on its left bank?
nindian-geography-2-11.x: The Hindan joins the Yamuna from the left; the Chambal, Sind, Betwa and Ken join from the right.

nindian-geography-1-19.s: The last left-bank tributary of the Ganga is the:
nindian-geography-1-19.x: The Mahananda is the last left-bank tributary and joins the Ganga in West Bengal.

nindian-geography-31-14.s: The Chambal Valley Project is located in:
nindian-geography-31-14.x: The Chambal Valley Project serves MP and Rajasthan; the Tungabhadra Project serves AP and Karnataka.

n33ef54543c2.s: The Indus enters the Arabian Sea near:
n33ef54543c2.x: The Indus flows between Ladakh and Zaskar, turns south at Nanga Parbat and meets the Arabian Sea near Karachi.

nc57ab85f711.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tungabhadra?
o: It is formed by the union of the Tunga and the Bhadra.
It is a left-bank tributary of the Krishna.
It joins the Krishna at Sangameswaram (Nandyal).
Vedavathi (Hagari) and Handri are its tributaries.
nc57ab85f711.x: The Tungabhadra is the largest right-bank tributary of the Krishna, not a left-bank one.

n56f1f5a4ff2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about rivers rising in the Aravallis?
o: The Luni ends in the Rann of Kutch.
The Banas is an east-flowing river.
The Sahibi is a south-flowing river.
The Sabarmati is a west-flowing river.
n56f1f5a4ff2.x: The Sahibi is a north-flowing river from the Aravallis, not south-flowing.

nap-geography-3-23.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sileru and the Sabari?
o: The Sileru joins the Sabari at the Andhra Pradesh-Telangana-Odisha tri-junction.
The upper reaches of the Sileru are called the Machkund.
The Sileru is a tributary of the Sabari.
The Sabari rises in the Sinkaram hill ranges of Odisha.
nap-geography-3-23.x: The Sileru meets the Sabari at the Andhra Pradesh-Chhattisgarh-Odisha tri-junction.

n6c746199c75.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about rivers that cross a line of latitude twice?
o: The Mahi crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.
The Congo crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.
The Limpopo crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice.
The Mahi drains into the Gulf of Khambhat.
n6c746199c75.x: The Congo crosses the Equator twice, not the Tropic of Cancer.

n3c488d00674.s:
Assertion (A): The Bist Doab lies between the Beas and the Sutlej.
Reason (R): The Chaj Doab lies between the Ravi and the Chenab.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n3c488d00674.x: Bist lies between the Beas and Sutlej, but the Chaj lies between the Chenab and Jhelum; the Ravi-Chenab doab is the Rechna.

ndd5697a78b9.s:
Assertion (A): Karnaprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Mandakini.
Reason (R): Rudraprayag is the confluence of the Alaknanda and the Mandakini.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ndd5697a78b9.x: Karnaprayag is the Alaknanda-Pindar confluence, so A is false; Rudraprayag is indeed the Alaknanda-Mandakini confluence.

nc5016042b76.s: Which State opposed the proposed Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar river link?
nc5016042b76.x: Telangana opposed the Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar link; climate change is also cited against the surplus-basin assumption.

nf5f2d4dca91.s: Kolleru, Andhra Pradesh's major lake, is a:
nf5f2d4dca91.x: Kolleru is a freshwater lake; Vembanad is a brackish backwater and Sambhar an inland saline lake.

nindian-geography-1-31.x: The Tapi rises at Multai in Betul district (MP) and flows west; Surat is near its mouth.

nbcefed74dc3.s: In 2018 the Supreme Court allocated 404.25 tmcft of Cauvery water to:
nbcefed74dc3.x: The 2018 verdict gave Tamil Nadu 404.25 tmcft and Karnataka 284.75 tmcft, and called the river a national asset.

n60135a297e1.s: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Godavari?
n60135a297e1.x: Pranhita, Indravati, Manjira and Kinnerasani are Godavari tributaries; the Ghataprabha is a tributary of the Krishna.

nba6bf167fa0.s: The Tapi flows through a rift valley between which ranges?
nba6bf167fa0.x: The Tapi's rift lies between the Satpura and Ajanta ranges; the Vindhya-Satpura rift belongs to the Narmada.

nap-geography-3-16.s: The biggest tributary of the Tungabhadra is the:
nap-geography-3-16.x: The Hagari (Vedavathi), rising in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, is the biggest tributary and joins near Siruguppa.

n6feb0fc580f.s: The Vamsadhara, Nagavali, Machkund, Sileru and Sabari rivers originate in the:
n6feb0fc580f.x: All five rivers originate in the Eastern Ghats.

n8c5652a0ac9.s: Which is described as the longest lake of India?
n8c5652a0ac9.x: Vembanad, a brackish backwater in Kerala, is the longest lake; Chilika is Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon.

nindian-geography-34-15.s: The largest artificial port of India is:
nindian-geography-34-15.x: Chennai is the largest artificial port; Mumbai is the largest natural port and Deendayal the largest by cargo.

nindian-geography-34-5.s: The largest salt-water lake of India is:
nindian-geography-34-5.x: Sambhar is the largest salt lake; Wular is the largest freshwater lake and Chilika the largest brackish lagoon.

nindian-geography-34-10.s: The largest river island of India is:
nindian-geography-34-10.x: Majuli in Assam is the largest river island.

nde7bd385278.s: The westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga is the:
nde7bd385278.x: The Yamuna is the westernmost and longest tributary of the Ganga; the Chambal and Betwa join it first.

n5bccdb63e7b.s: The Pranhita, the largest tributary of the Godavari, is formed by the Wardha and the:
n5bccdb63e7b.x: The Pranhita is formed by the Wardha and Wainganga and joins the Godavari near Kaleshwaram; the Manjira is a right-bank tributary.

nindian-geography-3-7.s: Kapildhara Falls near Amarkantak is on which river?
nindian-geography-3-7.x: Kapildhara is on the Narmada near Amarkantak in Anuppur; Hundru is on the Subarnarekha.

nindian-geography-1-29.s: The Kuakhai at Bhubaneswar is part of which river's delta?
nindian-geography-1-29.x: The Kuakhai is part of the Mahanadi delta; Cuttack also lies on the Mahanadi.

nindian-geography-3-6.x: Chitrakote is in Bastar; Dhuandhar is at Jabalpur and Dudhsagar in Goa.

n6a28e467b0c.s: The Godavari delta is known as the:
n6a28e467b0c.x: The Godavari delta is Konaseema, with seven distributaries including the Gautami, Vasishta and Vainateya.

nindian-geography-3-1.s: Jog Falls is on which river?
nindian-geography-3-1.x: Jog Falls is on the Sharavati; Chitrakote is on the Indravati and Dhuandhar on the Narmada.

nfff37640a5f.s: Aliabet is the largest island in which river?
nfff37640a5f.x: Aliabet is the largest island in the Narmada; Srirangam lies between the Kaveri and Kollidam.

n58f4a3067e5.s: The Baglihar dam is on which river?
n58f4a3067e5.x: Baglihar is on the Chenab; Pandoh is on the Beas.

n9bfcab5c9e1.s: The Kabini is a tributary of the:
n9bfcab5c9e1.x: The Kabini is a right-bank tributary of the Kaveri, not the Krishna.

nap-geography-3-8.s: Duduma Waterfalls is formed by which river?
nap-geography-3-8.x: The Machkund (Matsya Kundala) rises in the Madugula hills and forms Duduma Falls.

nindian-geography-37-17.x: Surajkund is in Haryana; Bhim Tal is in Uttarakhand and Uday Sagar in Rajasthan.

ne2f97a28dde.s: Which of the following is an example of an antecedent river?
ne2f97a28dde.x: Antecedent rivers such as the Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra rise in the Trans-Himalaya and cut gorges as ranges rise.

nindian-geography-1-6.x: The Krishna rises at Mahabaleshwar; the Godavari near Nashik, the Narmada at Amarkantak and the Tapi at Multai.

nindian-geography-37-2.s: Nakki Lake at Mount Abu is in:
nindian-geography-37-2.x: Nakki is in Rajasthan at Mount Abu; Badkhal is in Haryana and Ashtamudi in Kerala.

nba34541249c.s: Which river is regarded as India's longest river?
nba34541249c.x: The Ganga (2,525 km) is India's longest river; the Brahmaputra is longer overall but only 885 km lies in India.

nap-geography-4-9.s: The Vasishta branch of the Godavari meets the sea at:
nap-geography-4-9.x: The Vasishta meets the sea at Antarvedi; the Gautami at Yanam and the Vainateya at Komaragiripatnam.

nindian-geography-1-47.x: Lucknow is on the Gomati; Surat is on the Tapi and Jabalpur on the Narmada.

na2d076d8f35.s: The idea of interlinking India's rivers was first proposed in the 19th century by:
na2d076d8f35.x: Sir Arthur Cotton first proposed river linking in the 19th century; the 1980 National Perspective Plan is implemented through the NWDA.

nap-geography-2-7.s: In its upper reaches, the Sileru is known as the:
nap-geography-2-7.x: The Sileru rises in Andhra Pradesh, flows through Odisha and is called the Machkund in its upper course.

nbd1e622c69f.s: Hogenakkal Falls is on which river?
nbd1e622c69f.x: Hogenakkal, Sivasamudram and Chunchanakatte are all Kaveri waterfalls.

n2b2e2e4f63a.s: In May 2026, how did India respond to the Court of Arbitration's award under the Indus Waters Treaty?
o: It rejected the award as 'null and void'
It challenged the award at the ICJ
It referred the award to the World Bank
n2b2e2e4f63a.x: India rejected the award as 'null and void'; it has held the treaty in abeyance since 2025.

nindian-geography-1-38.s: The west-flowing Kali river of Karnataka rises near:
nindian-geography-1-38.x: The Kali rises near Diggi village in Uttara Kannada and flows west to the Arabian Sea.

nap-geography-3-12.s: Sir Arthur Cotton's anicut on the Godavari is at:
nap-geography-3-12.x: Cotton's anicut on the Godavari is at Dowleswaram; the river is 2.7 km wide at Rajahmundry.

nindian-geography-1-26.s: Nanded is situated on which river?
nindian-geography-1-26.x: Nanded is on the Godavari, which flows from Nashik through Maharashtra, Telangana and AP.

nindian-geography-3-4.s: Which waterfall on the Cauvery is noted for its large volume of water?
nindian-geography-3-4.x: Shivasamudram on the Cauvery carries a large volume; Jog on the Sharavati is noted for its width and Kunchikal for its height.

nindian-geography-1-42.s: Prayagraj is at the confluence of the Ganga and the:
nindian-geography-1-42.x: Prayagraj lies at the Ganga-Yamuna confluence; Varanasi, Patna and Bhagalpur are on the Ganga.

nindian-geography-34-16.s: The largest State of India by area is:
nindian-geography-34-16.x: Rajasthan is the largest State by area; Kutch is the largest district and Majuli the largest river island.

nindian-geography-1-30.s: Bhedaghat is located on which river?
nindian-geography-1-30.x: Bhedaghat, like Jabalpur and Kapildhara Falls, is on the Narmada.

nindian-geography-1-11.s: Ujjain is situated on which river?
nindian-geography-1-11.x: Ujjain is on the Kshipra; Hyderabad is on the Musi and Jagdalpur on the Indravati.

nindian-geography-2-6.s: Which of the following is a right-bank tributary of the Mahanadi?
nindian-geography-2-6.x: The Ong, Tel and Jonk join from the right; the Seonath, Hasdeo, Mand and Ib join from the left.

nindian-geography-3-11.s: Bhalkund (Rahatgarh) Falls in Madhya Pradesh is on which river?
nindian-geography-3-11.x: Bhalkund, also called Rahatgarh, is on the Bina in Madhya Pradesh, not on the Narmada.

nindian-geography-1-28.s: The Musi is a tributary of the:
nindian-geography-1-28.x: The Musi is a tributary of the Krishna, on which Vijayawada and Srisailam also lie.

nap-geography-3-14.s: Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna is located near:
nap-geography-3-14.x: Nagarjuna Sagar is near Nandikonda; Diviseema lies between the two Krishna branches.

n76b568b3aa8.s: The east-flowing rivers of Peninsular India generally form ____ at their mouths.
n76b568b3aa8.x: East-flowing rivers form large deltas on the Bay of Bengal; west-flowing rivers more commonly form estuaries.

n5d7b508c4d0.s: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which of the following rivers is allocated to India?
n5d7b508c4d0.x: The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej go to India; the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab mainly to Pakistan.

na9c21bbd198.s: Unlike Himalayan rivers, Peninsular rivers generally flow through:
na9c21bbd198.x: Peninsular rivers are usually seasonal and flow in broad, shallow graded valleys, while Himalayan rivers cut deep antecedent gorges.

na8b9c7c0b61.s: Which of the following is a right-bank tributary of the Godavari?
na8b9c7c0b61.x: Pravara, Manjira and Manair join the Godavari from the right; Purna, Pranahita, Indravati and Sabari join from the left.
